name: From Impressionism to Pop Art: Breaking the Rules
description: Each movement in modern art answered the one before it. Follow the artists, the isms and the pictures that moved painting from light on water to a soup can.

checkpoints.name: Prints and Paris
checkpoints.note: Japanese woodblock prints arrive in Europe, and young French painters begin to look at light and everyday life rather than history.

checkpoints.name: Light and colour
checkpoints.note: Impressionists and Post-Impressionists break with polished finish. Colour and feeling matter more than detail, and Art Nouveau spreads across design.

checkpoints.name: The age of isms
checkpoints.note: Expressionism, Cubism and Dada each break a rule, from realistic colour and a single viewpoint to the very idea of what art is.

checkpoints.name: Dreams and disaster
checkpoints.note: Surrealism, war and regional realism give painters new subjects, and Picasso paints a bombed town.

checkpoints.name: Pop and the market
checkpoints.note: Artists look at advertising, comics and film stars, and Abstract Expressionism gives way to Pop Art in New York.
